name: GitHub
description: Talk to this agent by @mentioning it in GitHub issue and pull-request comments — a GitHub App with webhook signature verification via eve's githubChannel.
setup:
This channel makes the agent a **GitHub App** — its `@mention` identity in issues and pull requests, and the credential it uses to work the repositories you install it on. Each agent needs its own App: two agents sharing a slug can't both hear their mentions.

**Guided (recommended):** after installing this channel, open the agent's **Deployment** tab and click **Create GitHub App**. harnesst registers the App on GitHub, stores its four secrets on the agent, and sends you to pick the repositories it watches. You can create it under your personal account or an organization you own.

**Manual:**

1. Create a **GitHub App** (Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps). Note its **App ID** → `GITHUB_APP_ID` and slug → `GITHUB_APP_SLUG` (the `@name` people mention).
2. Generate a **private key** (PEM) into `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, and set a **webhook secret** → `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
3. Deploy the agent, then set the App's **Webhook URL** to `https://<your-domain>/e/<environmentId>/eve/v1/github` (shown on the Deployment tab).
4. Subscribe to all four events the guided path subscribes to: **Issue comment**, **Issues**, **Pull request** and **Pull request review comment**. The two comment events carry `@mention`s; **Issues** and **Pull request** carry the label, open and push activity the wake rules below act on, so leaving them off makes those settings do nothing. Grant **Issues** and **Pull requests** read & write, and **Contents** read & write so the agent can clone, branch, and push.
5. Install the App on the repositories it should watch.

An issue or PR comment that `@mention`s the App's slug starts a turn.

**Waking without a mention.** The Deployment tab has a **GitHub channel settings** panel with three controls: the **repositories** this agent watches, the **wake labels** that rouse it, and whether a **new issue** wakes it. Until you name at least one repository the agent is inert — it answers mentions and nothing else — so installing or updating this channel never changes what an existing agent does.

Once configured, the agent wakes when a label lands on an issue or pull request in one of those repositories that carries a wake label, when a watched pull request gets new commits or leaves draft, and (if you turned it on) when an issue is opened or reopened. Removing a label, closing, editing or assigning never wakes it. (GitHub's webhook hands the channel the issue's label *snapshot* rather than the single label just added, so labelling an issue that already carries a wake label also wakes the agent — it reads its instructions, finds nothing new to do, and does nothing.) The agent also **never wakes on its own actions** — its own App applying a label is ignored, while another agent's is not, which is what lets two agents hand work back and forth without looping.

The wake labels don't have to exist in the repository yet; typing them here is usually how they get established. They are the trigger only — **what the agent should do about a label belongs in its instructions**, not here. The agent is told what happened ("pull request #19 labeled (`changes-requested` set)") and nothing about what to do; if its instructions don't cover that label, it will decide to do nothing.

**Questions the agent can't answer alone.** When the agent needs a human before it can continue, the question goes to your harnesst inbox — not to the issue thread. One question, one place to answer it: a copy on the thread could not be answered anyway, because a comment reply starts a NEW turn rather than resuming the one that is waiting. Answer it in harnesst and the agent picks up the same conversation and replies on the issue. (If the agent is running without a harnesst inbox to file to, or the filing fails, it falls back to posting the question on the thread so it is never simply lost.) That resume is delivered to an extra route this channel registers (`/eve/v1/github/harnesst/answer`), authenticated with the agent's own deployment token — a GitHub-homed session can only be resumed through the channel that owns it. Nothing to configure; harnesst wires it at deploy time.

**Reading the repository.** Every turn, the agent checks the repository out into its sandbox before it answers, using a short-lived installation token minted from the App credentials above. If that checkout fails it says so on the thread — a comment beginning "I could not check out …" means the reply under it was written **without** the code in front of it. (eve's own checkout brokers the token at the sandbox firewall, which the Docker sandbox harnesst deploys onto cannot do; it fails on every turn and swallows the error, so this channel does the checkout itself.)

**What you can edit.** Nothing in this channel's file. `agent/channels/github.ts` is the whole channel, and every update rewrites it from the template — an edit you make there is gone on the next update. Everything that varies per agent is configuration, not code: wake rules live on the Deployment tab, credentials are agent secrets, and what the agent should *do* about an event belongs in its instructions. If the channel file itself is wrong, that's one for an administrator.

A redeploy ends any conversation that was waiting on an answer: the session lives inside the container. Ask again on the issue to start a fresh one.

secrets.name: GITHUB_APP_ID
secrets.description: The GitHub App's numeric App ID. Set automatically by Create GitHub App on the Deployment tab.

secrets.name: GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
secrets.description: The GitHub App's private key (full PEM contents) — authenticates as the app to post replies and mint short-lived installation tokens for doing work. Set automatically by Create GitHub App.

secrets.name: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
secrets.description: The webhook secret configured on the App — eve verifies the inbound webhook signature against it. Set automatically by Create GitHub App.

secrets.name: GITHUB_APP_SLUG
secrets.description: The App's slug — the @name mentioned to trigger the agent. Set automatically by Create GitHub App (GitHub derives it from the final App name).
